entries.title: 2 John 1:1
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
a A general Name of Office fitly appropriated with Eminency here, he being the only Apostle, probably, now surviving on earth.

b This appears to have been some noted Person, whom both her her singular Pi[illegible]ty, and Rank in the World, made eminent, and capable of having great Influence for the support of the Christian Interest.

3 Joh. 1.

c Which her general Value with all that had known the Truth, (i. e. the Christians in those parts) shews. The Opinion that a Church is intended by this Appellation, had its greater probability, is of no great Importance; and needs not here be disputed.

entries.title: 2 John 1:2
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: d The indwelling of Evangelical Truth, which is here meant, signifies its deep Radication, and powerful transforming Efficacy in the Soul, so as to be productive of Holiness, as Iohn 17.17. than which nothing can be a greater Inducement among Christians of mutual Love.

entries.title: 2 John 1:3
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Gr. shall be.

Such Saluta[illegible]ns see explained, where they have formerly occurr'd.

entries.title: 2 John 1:4
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
f Some of her Sons, its probably conjectured, he had met with, upon their Occasions, at Ephesus, where, 'tis thought, he now resided, and found them to have a good Savour of Religion, and to walk according to Rule, which was matter of great Joy to him.

3 Joh. 3.

entries.title: 2 John 1:5
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
1 Joh. 3.11.

Joh. 13.34. & 15.12. Eph. 5.2. 1 Pet. 4.8. 1 Joh. 3.23.

g He inculcates that great Precept, of which see 1 Ioh. 2.7, 8.

entries.title: 2 John 1:6
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Joh. 15.10.

h From this particular Command, he passes to what is more general, requiring in all things a strict and unanimo[illegible]s adherence to the pure, and primitive Doctrine of the Gospel, which would be the best Expression of Love to God, and the true Center and Bond of [illegible]ove to one another, as 1 Ioh. 5.1, 3.

1 Joh. 2.24.

entries.title: 2 John 1:7
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines

entries.title: 2 John 1:8
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Gal. 3.4.

k Such changes of the Person, as we her[illegible] find, are neither unusual, nor in Exhortation, inelegant; but some Copies read in the two latter clauses [ye.] He presses to constancy in the true incorrupt Christian Profession.

Or, gained. Some Copies read, which ye have gained, but that ye rec[illegible]ive, &c.

l That the expected Recompence be not lost in the whole, or in any part, as Gal. 3.3, 4.

entries.title: 2 John 1:11
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: m Such as bring any contrary Doctrine, (as Gal. 1.8.) ought not to be harbour'd, or countenanced by any encouraging Salutation, lest we involve our selves in the Participation of their Guilt, 1 Tim. 5.22.

entries.title: 2 John 1:12
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
3 Joh. 13.

n The latter, write, is not in the Greek Text; but the words bear this sense, that having many things to write, I would not by Paper and Ink, impart them to you (the Expression being elliptical) but hope to come, &c.

Gr. mouth to mouth.

Joh. 17.13. 1 Joh. 1.4.

Or, your.

entries.title: 2 John 1:13
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
o They were, 'tis probable, with him at Ephesus, and took the occasion by him now writing, to transmit their Salutations.

p This concluding Amen imports his Sincerity in what he had written.
